title: Control Board Communication Fault
shortDescription: Communication failure between the main PCB and user interface board.
fullDescription:
F01 on Indesit dryers (Whirlpool EMEA platform) indicates the main electronic control cannot talk to the display/UI board or an auxiliary controller.

Most commonly caused by a loose ribbon cable, moisture on connectors, or a failed PCB. A 10-minute power cycle clears transient faults on many Indesit units.

causes.cause: Loose ribbon cable between PCB and display

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Remove top panel and reseat PCB ribbon cables.

fixSteps.title: Replace PCB
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the main control board if fault persists.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if reseating does not work.

title: Motor Tacho Signal Fault
shortDescription: Motor tachometer signal missing or invalid.
fullDescription:
F02 indicates the PCB cannot read motor speed feedback. The drum will either refuse to turn or stop after a few seconds.

Common causes: broken drive belt leaving motor unloaded, failed tacho coil, worn motor brushes, or damaged wiring.

fixSteps.title: Check belt
fixSteps.instruction: Rotate drum by hand and inspect belt.

fixSteps.title: Replace belt
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new drive belt around drum and pulley.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for motor replacement.

faq.q: Can a broken belt cause F02?
faq.a: Yes — the motor spins without load and gives no valid tacho reading.

title: NTC Sensor Fault
shortDescription: NTC temperature sensor reading out of range.
fullDescription:
F03 means the temperature thermistor is reporting an impossible value — usually open or shorted. The PCB stops the cycle to protect the load.

Replacement sensors are cheap and easy to fit; most DIYers can complete the repair in under an hour.

fixSteps.title: Access sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear panel to reach NTC near heater/condenser.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance (~10-50 kOhm at room temp) and swap if out of range.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if fault persists after sensor swap.

faq.q: Where is the NTC on my Indesit?
faq.a: Behind the rear panel, clipped to the heater housing or exhaust duct.

title: Pressure Switch Fault
shortDescription: Condensate pressure switch stuck or hose blocked.
fullDescription:
F04 indicates a fault in the condensate level sensing circuit. A full water tank, a kinked pressure hose, or a bad switch can all trigger it.

Start with the basics — empty the tank and ensure the hose is not kinked — before replacing parts.

fixSteps.title: Empty tank
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and empty the condensate tank.

fixSteps.title: Inspect hose
fixSteps.instruction: Check pressure hose for kinks or debris.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new pressure switch if hose is clear and switch does not click.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for sump work.

faq.q: Why is tank empty but F04 shows?
faq.a: A kinked hose can keep residual water pressure on the switch.

title: Drain Pump Fault
shortDescription: Condensate pump not moving water to the tank.
fullDescription: F05 indicates the condensate pump is blocked, failed, or not receiving drive signal. Clean the sump filter first — lint in the impeller is the most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Clean filter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean sump filter of all lint.

fixSteps.title: Access pump
fixSteps.instruction: Remove front panel to reach pump housing.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Test continuity (~180 ohms); replace if open.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for sealed sump designs.

faq.a: Yes, small fibres pass through the filter and wind around the impeller.

title: Door Lock Fault
shortDescription: Door interlock switch not confirming closed.
fullDescription: F06 indicates a failed door safety switch or catch alignment issue. Dryer refuses to start until resolved.

fixSteps.title: Close firmly
fixSteps.instruction: Press door firmly and listen for click.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for persistent wiring faults.

faq.a: Never — it is a legal safety device.

title: Heater Fault
fullDescription: F07 indicates the PCB is not seeing expected temperature rise. Most often a burnt heating element or tripped thermal cut-out, sometimes restricted airflow.

fixSteps.title: Reset TOC
fixSteps.instruction: Press manual reset button on thermal cut-out.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for heat-pump repairs.

faq.a: Usually the element or TOC has failed.

title: Heater Relay Stuck
shortDescription: Heater relay on PCB welded closed — safety fault.
fullDescription: F08 is a safety code raised when the PCB senses heater current with the relay commanded off. The dryer may overheat — unplug immediately and call a pro.
whenToCallPro: Always — F08 is a fire risk.

faq.a: No — unplug and call a technician.

title: Software ROM Error
shortDescription: Firmware integrity check failed at startup.
fullDescription: F09 indicates a corrupt firmware image on the PCB. A power cycle may clear transients; otherwise the board requires reprogramming or replacement.

faq.a: No — only service agents have access.

title: EEPROM Checksum Error
fullDescription: F10 appears when the EEPROM fails its internal checksum. Configuration data may be lost and the dryer refuses to operate until the PCB is replaced or re-initialised by service.

faq.a: Yes — default configuration must be reloaded by service.
